audit.whatIsWrong: Both chart layers gave Yasuo five stages and called the rest a coin flip, while the packet chart and all seven whys lines say Illaoi owns Level 1 through first item and only loses at two items.
audit.why: Illaoi wins 53.87% over 2183 games. Tentacle Smash reaches 850 against a 475 Steel Tempest, and Wind Wall is only 4 seconds of cover on a 25s rank-1 cooldown.
audit.corrected: Illaoi takes L1 through first item; Yasuo takes 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait the Wall' was repeated everywhere without ever printing the number that makes it actionable.
audit.why: Wind Wall lasts 4 seconds on a 25/23/21/19/17s cooldown. At rank 1 that is 21 seconds of lane where his answer to your E does not exist — and only 13 seconds at rank 5, which is why the two-item stage flips.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], late and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated the condition on Last Breath, and credited Illaoi's tentacles with beating an 'E-flow-shield' without saying how.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion.' Illaoi has no knock-up in her kit, so the only thing that puts you Airborne is his own two-stack Steel Tempest tornado — that stack count is the real tell for his all-in. Riot's passive text: the shield builds 'whenever he is moving' and triggers on damage, so repeated tentacle swings pop it and keep it down. Sweeping Blade also 'cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds', so his escape through you has gaps.
audit.corrected: All three written into spikes[1], early and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization prescribed 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern', and the late breakdown said 'anti-heal stays core'.
audit.why: Yasuo has no healing anywhere in his kit. Passive is a shield, Q, W, E and R carry no heal. Grievous Wounds does nothing in this matchup and the gold is wasted.
audit.corrected: report[8] and breakdown.late corrected — armour, not anti-heal.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged "Wind Wall's" — correct Riot name. False positive. The page does mix 'Wind Wall' and 'Windwall' spellings, which is cosmetic only.

edits.before: Once you have W Harsh Lesson to dash onto him, land E Test of Spirit through his Wind Wall's cooldown window; Windwall only blocks the tether for its brief uptime, so bait it or angle E when it's down. Ripping his spirit forces the classic choice: eat tentacle slams from your Q or die walking to his soul.
edits.after: Wind Wall lasts 4 seconds and is down 25 seconds at rank 1 — that gap is the whole lane. Bait it with a Q, count the 21 seconds it is gone, then Test of Spirit from 900 and Harsh Lesson onto the spirit every 4s. Ripping his soul forces the choice: eat tentacle slams, or walk away and become a Vessel.

edits.before: Your R Leap of Faith spawns a ring of tentacles that shred him even through E-flow-shield stacking. If he flashes in to all-in with his own ult knockup, you simply ult on top and every tentacle beats on him — his mobility can't dodge point-blank slams.
edits.after: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle for every champion it hits, and his Flow shield only builds while he is moving, so repeated swings pop it and hold it down. Last Breath needs an Airborne target and you have no knock-up — his own two-stack Steel Tempest tornado is what sets it up.

edits.before: With early Bramble/Sunfire plus your passive tentacle spawns off walls, extended trades are wildly one-sided; his Q1/Q2 pokes barely dent your tentacle-fed sustain. Any minion-wave shove lets you keep him zoned from CS.
edits.after: With your first item plus passive tentacle spawns off nearby walls, extended trades are one-sided: Steel Tempest is a 4s cooldown treated as a basic attack, and your tentacles heal you every time they connect with a champion. Keep him off CS.

edits.before: You out-stat Yasuo at level 1-2 with sturdier base HP and Q Tentacle Smash out-ranging his melee Q; he has no Windwall yet, so a clean E lands whenever he steps up to last-hit. Just avoid overwalking into a double-Q tornado poke.
edits.after: You out-stat Yasuo at 1-2 and Tentacle Smash (Q) reaches 850 against his 475 Steel Tempest; with no Wind Wall yet, a clean E lands whenever he steps up to last-hit. Avoid the double-Q tornado — that knock-up is what sets up his ult later.

edits.before: From 3 onward you own it: W lets you stick, E rips his spirit, and level 6 R drops a tentacle field he can't juke at close range. Force him to choose between farming and eating slams and his lane collapses.
edits.after: From 3 you own it: Harsh Lesson sticks on a 4s cooldown and Test of Spirit rips his spirit from 900. Sweeping Blade cannot re-dash the same target at once, so his escape has gaps — make him pick between farm and slams.

edits.before: Once Yasuo finishes crit items his Windwall reliably denies your E and his flanking mobility sidesteps tentacles, so close the game before his 2-item spike arrives.
edits.after: Once Yasuo finishes crit items Wind Wall is down only 17 seconds at rank 5 and his flanking mobility sidesteps tentacles, so close the game before his 2-item spike lands.

edits.before: Land E through a used or down Windwall
edits.after: Land E in the 21s after Wind Wall expires

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Yasuo has no healing in his kit — skip anti-heal here.

edits.before: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button — build your teamfight around that. Yasuo carry threat: 9/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button — build your teamfight around that. Yasuo carry threat: 9/10 — armour stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wind Wall and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 4.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wind Wall and how disciplined your pattern is.

notes: Wasted-gold error corrected: the page told the player to buy Executioner's Calling early because 'his healing fights your pattern'. Yasuo has no healing anywhere in his kit. Level chart in both layers contradicted the packet chart and every whys line; repaired in matched pairs. UNVERIFIED, left as the page already had it: whether Wind Wall blocks Test of Spirit. Illaoi's E carries no projectile flag in the kit data, so the data neither confirms nor denies it — but the entire page is built on that premise, so I did not disturb it.
